observation.visible_scene: A fixed, wide-angle (fisheye) night-vision / monochrome-yellow view of an outdoor test or launch site. A lattice water tower stands at left-center, a sloping rock/berm embankment runs along the lower right, and a flat foreground with thin poles and a fence line sits at the bottom. Dominating the center and right of the frame is a large incandescent fireball surrounded by billowing smoke clouds at the base and a few bright linear debris/rocket trails arcing upward. The water tower and rock berm remain in identical screen positions across all frames, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: The bright white-yellow core of the fireball steadily enlarges and its upper boundary rises over the ~2.7 s segment, transitioning from an irregular blob to a broad rounded dome that fills most of the upper-center frame (expansion, not translation of the whole scene).
The dense smoke masses at the left and bottom remain largely in place but are continuously re-illuminated and reshaped by the growing fireball behind them; their outer edges creep slightly outward.
The two upward streaking trails (one left of the tower, one upper-right) extend, thin, and fade relative to the brightening core; small bright specks (debris) scatter and drift across the upper sky.
Overall scene brightness increases as the fireball's glow washes over the foreground and water tower, with the tower's silhouette becoming less distinct against the brighter background smoke.
No camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident: background landmarks (tower, rocks, poles) hold constant screen positions throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or trigger of the fireball and what preceded the first frame are not shown; the explosion is already fully underway at t=0.
The outcome after the last frame (whether the fireball collapses, rises, or dissipates) is not shown.
The true identity of the bright trails (rockets, falling debris, or burning fragments) and the material composition of the fireball cannot be determined from the imagery alone.
uncertain_details: Whether the fireball's apparent rise is genuine upward translation of the burning mass or simply the expanding bright core overtaking the darker smoke below is not fully resolvable.
The thin upward streaks could be debris arcs or small rocket/ignition trails; their exact nature is ambiguous.
Minor edge shifts in the smoke clouds may be illumination changes rather than physical motion.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
